BIJLI BAZAAR (बिजली बाज़ार, "the electric market") is an invented three-night music festival: a night mela of bulbs, tent edges and hand-painted signs.BIJLI BAZAAR (बिजली बाज़ार, "the electric market") is an invented three-night music festival: a night mela of bulbs, tent edges and hand-painted signs.

Nine social posts announce it, each in 4:5 and 9:16, and no photograph does the work.

The challenge

Nine social posts, where every post solves a different layout problem:

  • A long headline, a number, a list, a quote and a date
  • A single object, a timetable, price tiers and a status change
  • Most festival feeds are one template with the text swapped, but a line-up, a date and a house rule are different shapes of information

The approach

The festival is the feed. One fixed system holds all nine posts together, while each post gets its own layout. A night mela is lit by bulbs, wires and hand-painted signs, so light is the type.

The details

  • Five named colours: Night, Rani, Genda, Mor and Kagaz
  • Two typefaces: Unbounded and Space Mono
  • Four type treatments, one per post: bulb marquee, sign-paint, tile-fill and misprint
  • Six fairground modules: chakri, genda, jhumka, bulbs, shamiana and ticket
  • A shamiana edge and a bilingual wordmark sign every post
  • Nine 9:16 Stories, recomposed rather than cropped

Concept project: the festival, its acts, dates and prices are fictional and have no connection to any real event.

how it landed

OutcomeOutcome

A concept project, so these are the results it is designed for, not live numbers.

What I delivered

  • Nine posts, each in 4:5 and 9:16: 18 artworks
  • A visual system: colours, type, four type treatments and six modules
  • A bilingual wordmark and monogram
  • A feed that reads as one long tent when posted in order

How I’d measure success

  • Can people read the date, the line-up and the prices at a glance
  • Saves and shares on the line-up and timetable posts
  • Is the feed recognised as one festival, even without the logo
  • Story taps through all nine posts

What it shows

  • Layout: a different answer for each kind of information
  • A system strict enough to hold nine different posts
  • Typography as the image, with no photographs
  • Indian craft references in a contemporary system
